gaps.name: The trace carries four families under one correlation id
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - renderTrace pairs lifecycle brackets on (phase, plan) and never consults corr, so a re-run closes the previous run's dangling dispatch and names the wrong worker unpaired; separately the live trace has never carried the lifecycle or outcome families
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/trace.mjs:238 builds the worker key as `${key(e.phase)} ${key(e.plan)}` and :240-247 push/shift on it with no corr in the key, contradicting the header's claim at :108-110 that a re-run starts a new id; live `trace render --phase 1` counts {routing:2, provider:9, lifecycle:0, outcome:0}
gaps.missing: include corr in the pairing key (and in unpaired[] entries) so brackets never cross runs; add a test with two runs of one phase at different shas asserting each run's dispatch pairs only within its own corr

gaps.name: A torn config layer is named, not silently defaulted
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the torn-layer arm is anchored to the repo layer's path, so a torn user-global layer produces neither ask nor deny
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/git-guard.mjs:110-111 filters warnings by the prefix `config layer <repoLayer> `, so a global-layer parse warning never reaches the arm at :148 even though that layer also carries protected_branches and on_protected
gaps.missing: match a parse warning from EITHER layer path (keeping the documented guard against the global path being a prefix of the repo path), and add a git-guard test with only the global layer truncated

gaps.name: lease-check refuses an undeclared staged path
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the staged-set read misses renames and mangles non-ASCII paths
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs:1441-1442 runs `git diff --cached --name-only` with no -z, no `-c core.quotePath=false` and no rename-source handling; the exact/prefix comparison at :1454-1456 then admits a rename that destroyed another plan's declared file, and refuses a declared `src/caf\303\251.js`
gaps.missing: read the staged set with `-z` (and `--name-status` or `-M` so a rename's SOURCE is checked too), then add two tests: a staged `git mv` out of another plan's lease returns ok:false, and a declared non-ASCII path returns ok:true

gaps.name: An executor staging an undeclared path halts
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the gate reads the whole staged index, so a file the USER pre-staged hard-blocks the phase
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs:1443-1456 compares every staged path against the plan's declared list with exactly one exemption (the plan's own report file, :1450); skills/cad-executor-contract/SKILL.md:73-75 turns any ok:false into a blocked checkpoint and :55-56 forbids the executor from touching staging it did not create
gaps.missing: scope the check to the paths this executor staged (or admit paths already staged at dispatch time and report them separately), and add a test where a pre-staged README.md leaves ok:true while an executor-staged undeclared path still fails

gaps.name: Lockfiles stop flooring a phase to critical
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - pnpm-lock.yaml, named in the item, still matches the concurrency surface
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/lib/risk-surfaces.mjs:65 `LOCKFILE_RE = /(?:\.lock|-lock\.json)$/i`; live matchSurfaces returns concurrency/critical for pnpm-lock.yaml and packages.lock.json while the other four return []
gaps.missing: widen the basename exclusion to `*-lock.*` (or name pnpm-lock.yaml / packages.lock.json explicitly) with a fixture per lockfile per D-21, since matchSurfaces returns at most one match per surface

gaps.name: A dropped reviewer is named in the trace
gaps.reason: unwired - the drop-outs most likely to fire throw before the trace event's `meta` exists, so nothing is written
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/review-provider.mjs:754-760 (review), :779-785 (consult), :810-818 (detect-models): resolveProvider (bad-provider :711, no-key :714) and assertUnderCap (over-cap :281) both fail() before `meta` is constructed, and the sole appendEvent call at :361 is reached only through meta
gaps.missing: build the trace context before the provider/cap checks (or emit the drop-out event from fail()'s path), and add tests asserting a provider event exists with the reason for no-key, bad-provider, bad-args, bad-payload and over-cap

gaps.name: decide refuses a milestone the repo already published
gaps.reason: behavior wrong - the comparison is against the highest semver tag rather than tag membership, so an untagged maintenance milestone is refused with a reason asserting a publication that never happened
gaps.evidence: cadence-core/bin/git-branch.mjs:96 passes highestSemverTag(readTags(dir)); lib/branch-decision.mjs:144-149 refuses on compareVersions <= 0. Live: decideBranch({integrationName:'cadence/v1.9.1', publishedVersion:'v2.0.0'}) -> ask/branch:null claiming 1.9.1 'has already published as a tag'
gaps.missing: pass the tag LIST (or a membership predicate) and refuse only when the milestone's own version is present among the tags; add a test for v1.9.1 in a repo tagged v1.9.0 and v2.0.0 returning create/ask on the branch name

human_checks.name:
In a scratch repo carrying a lint script and NO .planning/config.json, dispatch a cad-executor on a task whose edit fails that lint.
1. `cd` to a throwaway repo with `package.json` scripts.lint that fails on the edited file and no `.planning/config.json`.
2. Run `node /data/code/cadence/cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs detect-commands --root .` and confirm `"lint":"npm run lint"`.
3. Dispatch a cad-executor on a plan task whose edit fails that lint.
4. Run `git log --oneline -1` afterwards.
human_checks.expected: The executor makes three bounded attempts, returns a `blocked` checkpoint naming the lint failure, and step 4 shows NO commit for that task.
human_checks.why_human: The three-attempt bound and the blocked disposition live in executor contract prose (skills/cad-executor-contract/SKILL.md, <deviation_rules> carve-out per D-13); nothing in the tree can exercise a dispatch. Note while running it: detect-commands names a binary without checking it is reachable and the eslint arm emits `npx eslint .`, so a repo without the named tool is the adjacent case worth observing.

human_checks.name:
Dispatch a cad-executor on this machine, which has no code-intelligence plugin installed.
1. Run `node /data/code/cadence/cadence-core/bin/self-verify.mjs` and confirm `ok:true`.
2. Dispatch any cad-executor task (either rung).
3. Watch the dispatch's first turn for a tools-frontmatter error.
human_checks.expected: The dispatch completes normally; the unrecognized `LSP` entry is ignored rather than erroring the agent.
human_checks.why_human: This is an empirical claim about the running host, flagged as an assumption in CONTEXT.md; the declaration halves are already verified statically (agents/cad-executor*.md:4, self-verify.mjs:182).

human_checks.name:
After the next `/cad-execute`, read the trace.
1. Run `node /data/code/cadence/cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs trace render --phase <that phase>`.
2. Read `counts` and `unpaired`.
3. Confirm every event shares one `corr`.
human_checks.expected: All four counts (routing, provider, lifecycle, outcome) are non-zero, every event carries the same `corr`, and `unpaired` is empty.
human_checks.why_human: The lifecycle and outcome producers are orchestrator prose added by this phase, so they could not fire during the run that built it - today's file shows lifecycle:0 and outcome:0. Only a fresh run whose orchestrator loaded the new execute.md can produce the record.

human_checks.name:
Run /cad-health against a tree whose PROJECT.md ### Active version does NOT sort above what it has shipped.
1. Copy a planning tree to scratch and set `### Active` to a version at or below the newest `git tag --list` entry.
2. Run `/cad-health` there.
3. Read the issue list.
human_checks.expected: Check 7 reports a version drift naming BOTH numbers and which comparand answered.
human_checks.why_human: D-24 makes the rule prose-only this phase (skills/cad-health/SKILL.md:72-80), so there is no seam to exercise, and this repo carries no drift (Active v2.5.0, newest tag v2.4.0).
